In partnership with
June Kailes
, The Partnership developed transit evacuation planning guidance and a checklist for emergency managers, planners, and individuals to use when evaluating current evacuation plans, preparing for disaster events, and creating personal preparedness evacuation plans.
The Partnership, in collaboration with
Justice Shorter of SeededGround
and June Kailes, also provides the Roadmap as a resource for inclusive transportation evacuation planning.
If you have any accessibility questions or concerns, please contact Priya Penner at
priya@disasterstrategies.org
.
National Resources
For Emergency Managers and Planners
Transit Guidance – Key Integration Details
Progress Tracking Document
How to use the Tracking Progress document alongside the Transit Guidance:
Follow the Transit Guidance and evaluate your current status using the accompanying Progress Tracking Document.
A Roadmap: Making Transportation Evacuations Real for People with Disabilities
This roadmap is a concise yet clear summary of reflections, report outs, and recommendations shared throughout two Transportation Evacuation Think Tank sessions held in February 2025.
For Individual Preparedness
Disability Emergency Personal Evacuation Transportation Planning
This planning guidance and checklist is a tool for individuals to use when getting ready for disaster events and creating and maintaining personal preparedness evacuation plans.
Recording: Strengthening Transit Evacuation Plans
Presented: September 25, 2025
View the recording as we:
Introduce new “how-to” tools and guidance.
Discuss some key transit evacuation lessons from the January 2025 Los Angeles fires and how to use them as opportunities to identify and address planning gaps.
Provide examples of both weak and strong planning solutions that increase precision, clarity, and accountability in messaging, response, and personal planning.
